question: Which of the following is NOT a method typically involved in soft tissue techniques?
cited_learning_objective: Identify the method that is not a soft tissue technique.

options.rationale: Lateral stretching is a soft tissue method.
Deep pressure is a soft tissue method.
Traction is a soft tissue method.

options.text: Separation of muscle origin and insertion
options.rationale: Separating origin and insertion is a soft tissue method.
Soft tissue techniques include lateral or linear stretching, deep pressure, traction, and separation of the muscle origin and insertion. HVLA thrusts are not a soft tissue technique.

question: Which of the following is an absolute contraindication for soft tissue techniques?
cited_learning_objective: Identify an absolute contraindication to soft tissue.

options.rationale: A fracture is an absolute contraindication because applying soft tissue to the area can aggravate the injury and delay healing.
DVT is treated later in this packet as a relative contraindication. The printed choice omitted the parentheses.
The packet says the conditions other than fracture may be relative contraindications that require caution.
Neoplasm is not the absolute contraindication keyed in this item.
Hypertonic muscles are a reason to use soft tissue, not an absolute contraindication.

question: The Bilateral Cervical Extensor Muscle Stretch lengthens the cervical extensors by drawing their origin and insertion apart along the long axis of the muscle, using the physician's crossed forearms as a forward-bending fulcrum. This method is best classified as which of the following?
cited_learning_objective: Classify the Bilateral Cervical Extensor Muscle Stretch.

options.rationale: A perpendicular or bow-string stretch pulls across the long axis, not along it.
Effleurage is light gliding, not this end-to-end stretch.
A longitudinal stretch applies traction along the long axis, separating origin from insertion. The Bilateral Cervical Extensor Muscle Stretch does this to the cervical extensors.
Petrissage is kneading or squeezing.
Tapotement is rhythmic percussion, not a stretch.

question: Which of the following is a relative contraindication for soft tissue techniques?
cited_learning_objective: Identify a relative contraindication to soft tissue.

options.rationale: Fracture is an absolute contraindication in this packet.
An open wound is not the relative contraindication keyed here.

DVT is a relative contraindication because force in the area can dislodge a clot and cause embolic complications. Treatment may proceed in other regions, but local treatment around a clot must be avoided. The printed choice omitted the parentheses.
Infection is not the relative contraindication keyed in this item.
Abscess is not the relative contraindication keyed in this item.

question: Which of the following is a benefit of soft tissue techniques?
cited_learning_objective: Identify a benefit of soft tissue technique.

options.rationale: Soft tissue decreases muscle tension.
Decreased mobility is not a stated benefit.
Soft tissue enhances blood and lymphatic flow, aiding nutrient delivery, oxygen exchange, and removal of metabolic waste.
Impaired immune response is not a stated benefit.
Increased stress is not a stated benefit.

question: A soft tissue technique applies a medial-to-lateral force across the erector spinae muscles, displacing them away from the spinous processes. This force is most accurately described as which of the following?
cited_learning_objective: Classify a medial-to-lateral erector spinae force.

options.rationale: Effleurage is a massage stroke, not this transverse displacement.
A longitudinal stretch would pull along the axis.
A perpendicular stretch applies force across the long axis. Displacing the erector spinae medial to lateral crosses the fiber direction.
Petrissage is a massage stroke, not this transverse displacement.
A rotatory stretch is not the standard descriptor for this transverse displacement.

question: What is the primary difference between osteopathic soft tissue techniques and similar manual treatments developed outside the osteopathic profession?
cited_learning_objective: State what distinguishes osteopathic soft tissue.

options.rationale: The mechanical techniques are often similar to other manual therapies.

options.text: The focus on muscles, fascia, and connective tissues
options.rationale: That tissue focus is shared with other manual therapies.

options.text: The treatment of specifically diagnosed somatic dysfunctions
options.rationale: Osteopathic soft tissue is directed at treating diagnosed somatic dysfunctions. That diagnostic framework is the defining distinction.

options.text: The use of lateral or linear stretching
options.rationale: Lateral or linear stretching is not the distinction keyed here.
Improving circulation is not the distinction keyed here.

question: A positive standing flexion test on the left is no longer present after treatment with the left Unilateral Thoracic and Lumbar Paraspinal Soft Tissue Pressure and Stretch, Lateral Recumbent with Counterforce technique. Which of the following is the most plausible explanation?
cited_learning_objective: Explain a standing flexion test that resolves after lumbar soft tissue.

options.text: The technique reduced left hamstring muscle tone
options.rationale: Reducing left hamstring tone would tend to let the left PSIS ride superiorly rather than normalize the test.

options.text: The technique decreased left erector spinae muscle tone
options.rationale: A standing flexion test can be falsely positive when the lumbar musculature on that side is hypertonic. Reducing left erector spinae tone resolves that falsely positive finding.

options.text: The technique increased motion at the pubic symphysis
options.rationale: The technique does not meaningfully change the pubic symphysis.

options.text: The technique reduced left sacroiliac joint motion
options.rationale: The technique would tend to increase, not decrease, left sacroiliac motion.

options.text: Longitudinal stretch of the paraspinals resolved the dysfunction
options.rationale: The technique uses a transverse stretch, not a longitudinal one.

question: Which of the following is NOT a proposed mechanism of soft tissue techniques?
cited_learning_objective: Identify a mechanism that is not proposed for soft tissue.

options.rationale: Muscle relaxation is a proposed mechanism.
Increased flexibility is a proposed mechanism.
Improved circulation is a proposed mechanism.
Reflex modulation is a proposed mechanism.
There is no evidence in this packet that these techniques suppress immune function.

question: How are diagnosis and treatment performed simultaneously using soft tissue techniques?
cited_learning_objective: Describe simultaneous diagnosis and treatment.

options.text: By applying treatment force while sensing changes in the tissues
options.rationale: The physician palpates as force is applied and senses tone, tension, and changes in movement.

options.text: By using imaging techniques during treatment
options.rationale: Imaging is not how this packet describes simultaneous diagnosis and treatment.

options.text: By monitoring the patient's heart rate and blood pressure
options.rationale: Vital signs are not the method described.

options.text: By asking the patient for feedback during treatment
options.rationale: Patient report is not the method keyed for simultaneous diagnosis.

options.text: By using specialized equipment to measure tissue changes
options.rationale: Specialized equipment is not the method described.

question: A physician applies rhythmic, repetitive percussive tapping to the patient's paraspinal musculature. This is most accurately described as which of the following?
cited_learning_objective: Name rhythmic percussive tapping.

options.rationale: Skin rolling lifts and rolls skin between the thumb and fingers.
Effleurage is light, gentle, superficial circular gliding.
Kneading, or petrissage, is deep stretching, kneading, or squeezing.
Tapotement consists of rhythmic percussive tapping movements.
Direct inhibition is steady, sustained, deep pressure held on the tissue.

question: What is the importance of diagnosing somatic dysfunction during soft tissue technique treatment?
cited_learning_objective: State why diagnosis during soft tissue treatment matters.

options.text: It allows for simultaneous diagnosis and treatment
options.rationale: This is true, but it is not the only correct statement.

options.text: It helps identify areas of restricted motion
options.rationale: This is true, but it is not the only correct statement.

options.text: It ensures the technique is applied appropriately
options.rationale: This is true, but it is not the only correct statement.
A and B are both true, and C is also true.
Soft tissue allows simultaneous diagnosis and treatment, helps identify restricted motion, and ensures the technique is applied appropriately.

question: While performing the prone Unilateral Thoracic and Lumbar Paraspinal Soft Tissue Pressure with Transverse Stretch in the lumbar region, the physician's superior hand presses the paraspinals anteriorly and laterally, and the inferior hand grasps and lifts the anterior superior iliac spine away from the table. What is the purpose of that lift with the inferior hand?
cited_learning_objective: State the purpose of the ASIS lift in the prone lumbar stretch.

options.rationale: Any abdominal stretch is incidental, not the purpose.

options.text: Lateral stretch of the hip flexors
options.rationale: Hip flexors are not stretched in this technique.

options.text: Enhancing lumbar rotation to the left
options.rationale: The maneuver induces the opposite direction of lumbar rotation from the side being lifted.

options.text: Direct inhibition at the anterior superior iliac spine
options.rationale: There is no direct inhibition in this technique.

options.text: Providing counterforce for the lumbar stretch
options.rationale: Lifting the ASIS provides a counterforce against the superior hand so it can engage the tissue barrier and produce a transverse lumbar stretch.

question: Which of the following is a tip for successful treatment with soft tissue techniques when dealing with patients who present with contraindications?
cited_learning_objective: Choose the safe response to a contraindication.

options.text: Apply the technique regardless of the contraindication
options.rationale: Contraindications must always be considered.

options.text: Exercise caution and assess the appropriateness of the technique
options.rationale: If soft tissue is still a possibility, it should be used only with great caution and careful clinical judgment.

options.text: Ignore the contraindication and focus on the patient's comfort
options.rationale: Ignoring a contraindication is not the packet's advice.

options.text: Apply more force to overcome the contraindication
options.rationale: More force is not the response to a contraindication.

options.text: Treat the contraindication with a different technique first
options.rationale: That sequence is not the tip keyed here.

question: Which of the following is NOT a tip for successful treatment with soft tissue techniques?
cited_learning_objective: Identify a practice that is not a successful soft tissue tip.

options.rationale: Consent and comfort are tips for successful treatment.

options.text: Simultaneously diagnosing and treating somatic dysfunction
options.rationale: Simultaneous diagnosis and treatment is a tip in this packet.

options.text: Applying excessive force to achieve faster results
options.rationale: Successful soft tissue uses gentle, patient-appropriate pressure. Excessive force risks tissue damage and discomfort.

options.text: Assessing the appropriateness of the technique in specific clinical circumstances
options.rationale: Assessing appropriateness is a tip.

options.text: Exercising caution when dealing with patients who present with contraindications
options.rationale: Caution with contraindications is a tip.

question: Which of the following lab techniques employs a lateral or transverse stretch as its primary method?
cited_learning_objective: Select the technique that is a lateral stretch.

options.text: A supine technique that lifts the head into forward bending to lengthen the cervical extensors end to end
options.rationale: Lifting the head into forward bending is a longitudinal stretch.

options.text: A supine technique that holds steady pressure in the suboccipital space until the tissue softens
options.rationale: Steady suboccipital pressure is direct inhibition.

options.text: A prone technique using rhythmic percussion over the thoracic paraspinals
options.rationale: Rhythmic percussion is tapotement, not a stretch.

options.text: A lateral recumbent lumbar technique that displaces the paraspinals away from the spine against a counterforce
options.rationale: Displacing the lumbar paraspinals away from the spine against a counterforce is a lateral or transverse stretch.

options.text: An upper extremity technique that holds sustained pressure on a hypertonic levator scapulae band
options.rationale: Sustained pressure on the levator scapulae is direct inhibition.

question: Provide a brief description of skin rolling, effleurage, tapotement, and petrissage.
cited_learning_objective: Describe skin rolling, effleurage, tapotement, and petrissage.
answer: Skin rolling lifts the skin away from deeper structures and rolls the skin fold along the body. Effleurage is a light stroking movement, often used to promote lymphatic drainage. Tapotement is rhythmic striking, often with the side of the hand. Petrissage is kneading of muscles to mobilize tissue and improve circulation.
rationale: These are the packet's descriptions of the four techniques.

question: A physician sits at the head of the table, cradles the occiput with crossed forearms, and gently lifts the head into forward bending until a firm barrier is reached, producing traction along the cervical paraspinal muscles. Which soft tissue method is being applied?
cited_learning_objective: Classify cervical traction from a head-of-table lift.

options.rationale: Direct inhibition is sustained pressure on a hypertonic point without traction.
Lifting the head to separate origin from insertion applies traction along the long axis, which is a longitudinal stretch.
A perpendicular stretch would push across the muscle belly rather than lengthen it end to end.
Skin rolling engages superficial tissue only.
Tapotement is percussion.

question: A 57-year-old woman describes constant tension between her shoulders that worsens at work. She works as a paralegal and spends most of her time at a desk or looking through filing cabinets. Examination shows tenderness and hypertonicity throughout her cervical and thoracic paraspinal muscles. Three years ago she fractured her femur in a motor vehicle accident and later developed a DVT. She reports being well recovered and is not taking prescription medications. After consent, you decide to begin with soft tissue techniques. Soft tissue techniques are:
cited_learning_objective: Judge whether soft tissue is indicated after a remote femur fracture and DVT.

options.rationale: The previous fracture was in the lower extremity and has resolved. The history given is a femur fracture, not a current compression fracture.

Soft tissue is indicated for the cervical and thoracic somatic dysfunction. The previous fracture and DVT have resolved and are no longer contraindications. She is not on anticoagulants. Age alone is not an indication.
The DVT was remote and has resolved.
She is not taking prescription medications, including anticoagulants.
Specific ages are not indications for soft tissue techniques.

question: Which of the following best describes the location and direction of the force applied during the prone Unilateral Thoracic and Lumbar Paraspinal Soft Tissue Pressure with Transverse Stretch technique?
cited_learning_objective: Locate the contact and force of the prone transverse stretch.

options.text: Lateral to the erector spinae, directed anterior and medial
options.rationale: Contacting lateral to the muscle and pushing medially does not describe this technique.

options.text: Medial to the erector spinae, directed anterior and lateral
options.rationale: The contact is medial to the bulk of the erector spinae, and the force is anterior and lateral, producing a transverse stretch.

options.text: Posterior to the rhomboids, directed anterior
options.rationale: Contacting the rhomboids does not describe this technique.

options.text: Medial to the rhomboids, directed lateral
options.rationale: The rhomboids are not the contact for this transverse stretch.

options.text: Lateral to the paraspinals, directed medial
options.rationale: A lateral contact directed medially is the opposite of this technique.

question: An 89-year-old man fell while crossing a threshold and caught himself with his left hand. He has sharp pain and difficulty moving the wrist. Exam shows distress, bruising and swelling of the distal forearm and wrist, motion limited by pain, a dorsiflexed wrist, and tenderness at the radial head. Soft tissue technique is:
cited_learning_objective: Decide on soft tissue when fracture is suspected.

options.rationale: Somatic dysfunction does not outweigh the absolute contraindication of a suspected fracture.

options.text: Indicated for the improvement of local circulation and healing
options.rationale: Circulation and healing do not outweigh a suspected fracture.
The history and exam make a radius or wrist fracture likely. Fracture is an absolute contraindication.
Swelling is not a contraindication to soft tissue.

options.text: Contraindicated due to the restricted range of motion
options.rationale: Restricted range of motion is not a contraindication to soft tissue.

question: During a prone thoracic treatment, the physician pushes the paraspinal muscle mass laterally, at a right angle to the direction of its fibers. What term best describes this stretch?
cited_learning_objective: Name a force applied at a right angle to the fibers.

options.rationale: Force applied at a right angle to the fiber direction is a transverse, or perpendicular, stretch.
A longitudinal stretch runs parallel to the fibers, lengthening origin to insertion.
Effleurage is a light gliding stroke.
Direct inhibition is sustained pressure on a hypertonic point.
Tapotement is rhythmic percussion.

question: On physical examination, a 25-year-old man has a flexed occipitoatlantal joint that freely translates to the right. The physician cradles the occiput, places her fingertips below it to contact the area of C1, and applies a gentle sustained superior force with a slight anterior force. The technique described is an example of:
cited_learning_objective: Classify suboccipital superior and anterior force.

options.rationale: A longitudinal stretch focuses on a single muscle or set of muscles that move a joint in one direction. This technique focuses on myofascial structures and multiple muscles.
A transverse stretch keeps origin and insertion fixed while the central portion is stretched perpendicular to its long axis. The lateral component here is not perpendicular.
Traction longitudinally pulls apart the origin and insertion of the targeted myofascial structures, which matches this superior and slight anterior force.
Direct inhibition applies sustained deep pressure. Pressure here is used gently and is not the classification.

question: A 19-year-old man has neck tension after studying for finals on a laptop for a week. Exam shows suboccipital and cervical paraspinal hypertonicity and numerous segmental cervical somatic dysfunctions. After consent, treatment starts with the Bilateral Cervical Extensor Muscle Stretch. This technique may be applied:
cited_learning_objective: State how the Bilateral Cervical Extensor Muscle Stretch may be applied.

options.rationale: A sustained stretch is one correct use, but not the only one.

options.text: As a kneading or rhythmic motion
options.rationale: Kneading or rhythmic motion is one correct use, but not the only one.

options.text: To prepare before other techniques and further treatment
options.rationale: Preparatory use is correct, but not the only correct use.
This technique can be applied as a sustained stretch, rhythmic kneading, or preparatory treatment.
The listed applications are all correct.

question: A student wants to practice a direct inhibition technique. Which of the following best fits that method?
cited_learning_objective: Select an example of direct inhibition.

options.text: Lengthening the cervical extensors along their long axis with a forward-bending fulcrum
options.rationale: That is a longitudinal stretch.

options.text: Holding sustained, deep pressure on a hypertonic levator scapulae until it releases
options.rationale: Sustained deep pressure on a hypertonic muscle until it releases is direct inhibition.

options.text: Displacing the lumbar paraspinals laterally away from the spine
options.rationale: That is a transverse stretch.

options.text: Applying rhythmic percussive tapping to the thoracic paraspinals
options.rationale: That is tapotement.

options.text: Pulling the posterior cervical tissues superiorly with longitudinal traction
options.rationale: That is a longitudinal stretch.

question: A 45-year-old male accountant has discomfort in his right forearm, with tension during pronation, supination, wrist flexion, and extension. Exam shows limited pronation and supination and palpable tension along the forearm musculature. Which soft tissue technique is most indicated?
cited_learning_objective: Choose the soft tissue technique for forearm tension.

options.text: Bilateral Posterior Cervical Soft Tissue Pressure with Traction
options.rationale: A cervical technique does not directly target the forearm dysfunction described.
Rib raising does not directly target the forearm. The printed choice omitted the opening parenthesis.

options.text: Bilateral Bidirectional Paraspinal Soft Tissue Pressure and Longitudinal Stretch
options.rationale: A paraspinal stretch does not directly target the forearm dysfunction described.

options.text: Direct Soft Tissue Treatment of Scars
options.rationale: Scar treatment is not the technique keyed for this forearm tension.

options.text: Inhibitory Pressure with Stretching of the Forearm and Interosseous Membrane
options.rationale: This technique directly targets the forearm and is the most indicated of the listed choices.

question: A student notes that a patient's positive left standing flexion test disappears immediately after left lumbar transverse-stretch soft tissue treatment. Which mechanism best accounts for the change?
cited_learning_objective: Explain resolution of a left standing flexion test after lumbar soft tissue.

options.rationale: The pubic symphysis is not the driver here.

options.text: Reduced tone in the left lumbar erector spinae that had produced a false positive
options.rationale: Ipsilateral lumbar hypertonicity can cause a falsely positive standing flexion test. Reducing left erector spinae tone removes the false positive.

options.text: Increased tone of the right hamstrings
options.rationale: Increasing right hamstring tone would worsen, not resolve, a right-sided contribution.

options.text: Fusion of the left sacroiliac joint
options.rationale: Soft tissue treatment does not fuse the sacroiliac joint.

options.text: Stretching of the left iliopsoas along its long axis
options.rationale: The iliopsoas is not the muscle targeted by lumbar paraspinal soft tissue.

question: A 27-year-old woman has pain in her right neck and shoulder after moving and carrying boxes for two weeks. Exam shows hypertonicity of the levator scapulae, with a discrete area of tenderness and significant tension. Which technique is most indicated?
cited_learning_objective: Choose treatment for a discrete hypertonic band in levator scapulae.

options.rationale: A hypertonic muscle with a discrete area of maximal tension is treated with direct inhibition.

options.text: Muscle energy to the lumbar spine
options.rationale: Lumbar muscle energy does not treat the levator scapulae finding described.
Rib HVLA does not treat the finding described.
Forearm balanced ligamentous tension does not treat the finding described.
The packet does not contraindicate OMM for this finding.

question: Which soft tissue method may interrupt a cycle of muscle spasm through rhythmic percussion that alters neurologic feedback to the spinal cord?
cited_learning_objective: Name the percussive method that can interrupt spasm.

options.rationale: Effleurage is light gliding, not percussion.
Tapotement is the percussive method that can break a spasm cycle by stimulating or inhibiting neurologic firing that regulates muscle.
Petrissage is kneading, not percussion.
Skin rolling engages superficial tissue and is not percussive.
A longitudinal stretch applies traction along the muscle axis and is not percussive.

question: A frail 65-year-old woman with kyphosis has had back pain for several years. She is fidgety and anxious because the last time she was in a medical office her husband was diagnosed with cancer. Exam shows hypertonic muscles throughout her back and multiple areas of dysfunction. Why would soft tissue be a good choice to begin with?
cited_learning_objective: Explain why soft tissue is a starting technique for this patient.

options.text: To help her relax and feel more comfortable in the office
options.rationale: This is one reason, but not the only one.
This is one reason, but not the only one.
This is one reason, but not the only one.
This is one reason, but not the only one.
Soft tissue is gentle, safe for older patients, reduces muscle tension, is generally well tolerated, and can help anxious patients feel more at ease.

question: In the prone lumbar technique, the superior hand engages the paraspinal barrier with anterolateral pressure. Removing the inferior hand's lift on the ASIS would most likely have which effect?
cited_learning_objective: Predict the effect of removing the ASIS counterforce.

options.text: The physician would lose the counterforce needed to engage the tissue barrier effectively
options.rationale: The inferior hand supplies the counterforce that lets the superior hand reach and hold the tissue barrier.

options.text: The technique would convert to a longitudinal stretch
options.rationale: Removing the lift does not convert the method to a longitudinal stretch.

options.text: The hip flexors would be directly inhibited
options.rationale: Removing the lift does not inhibit the hip flexors.
The technique is a transverse stretch, not a sidebending block.

options.text: The abdominal wall would be the primary tissue treated
options.rationale: Removing the lift does not make the abdominal wall the primary target.

question: A 57-year-old restaurant manager has low back pain. You find somatic dysfunction in both the lumbar and sacral spine and want to begin with lumbosacral traction. In what direction is the force of the physician's superior hand?
cited_learning_objective: State the superior-hand force in lumbosacral traction.

options.rationale: Inferior force is not the superior-hand direction.
Medial-to-lateral force is not the superior-hand direction.
Lateral-to-medial force is not the superior-hand direction.
The superior hand applies anterior and cephalad pressure at the lumbar spine. The inferior hand applies anterior and caudal pressure at the sacrum, decompressing the lumbosacral junction.
Posterior and caudal is not the superior-hand direction.

question: A physician performing the prone Unilateral Paraspinal Soft Tissue Pressure with Transverse Stretch places the contact medial to the paraspinal mass. In which direction should the force be applied to create the intended transverse stretch?
cited_learning_objective: Choose the force direction from a medial paraspinal contact.

options.rationale: From a medial contact, anterior and lateral force displaces the paraspinals away from the spine.
Posterior and medial force would push toward the spine and lift away from the tissue.
A purely superior force would create a longitudinal effect.
A purely inferior force would create a longitudinal effect.
Anterior and medial force would not displace the muscle laterally.

question: Which of the following best defines soft tissue osteopathic manipulative treatment (ST)?
cited_learning_objective: Define soft tissue OMT.

options.text: A technique focused on bone alignment
options.rationale: Bone alignment is not the definition of soft tissue.

options.text: A direct, hands-on technique applied to muscles, fascia, and connective tissues
options.rationale: Soft tissue OMT directly applies stretching, pressure, or traction to muscles, fascia, and connective tissues. The printed stem omitted the parentheses around ST.

options.text: A passive technique that relies on patient muscle contraction
options.rationale: Patient muscle contraction is not the definition of soft tissue.

options.text: A cranial technique aimed at cerebrospinal fluid flow
options.rationale: Cranial technique is not the definition of soft tissue.

options.text: A technique that uses only high-velocity thrusts
options.rationale: High-velocity thrusts are not soft tissue.

question: Which soft tissue method separates the origin and insertion of a muscle group from one another through a traction force generated by the physician along the muscle's long axis?
cited_learning_objective: Name the stretch that separates origin and insertion.

options.rationale: Effleurage is a massage stroke, not end-to-end traction.
Petrissage is a massage stroke oriented to the muscle belly.
A perpendicular stretch crosses the long axis.
Tapotement is percussive.
A longitudinal stretch applies traction along the long axis, drawing origin and insertion apart.

question: Soft tissue techniques influence which of the following tissue systems?
cited_learning_objective: List the tissue systems influenced by soft tissue.

options.rationale: The effect is broader than muscle and fascia.
Muscle and fascia are also included.
Soft tissue is not limited to skeletal structures.

options.text: Fascial, muscular, lymphatic, vascular, and neural
options.rationale: Soft tissue improves muscular and fascial tone, lymphatic and vascular flow, and modulates neural reflexes.
The effect is not limited to skin and subcutaneous tissue.

question: Which of the following best describes how soft tissue is often employed with other OMT techniques?
cited_learning_objective: State how soft tissue is used with other OMT.

options.text: It is never used with other OMT approaches
options.rationale: Soft tissue is used with other approaches.

options.text: It is used only after HVLA
options.rationale: It is not limited to use after HVLA.

options.text: It is used to prepare tissues for other types of manipulation
options.rationale: Soft tissue can relax and mobilize tissues so later HVLA, muscle energy, or articulatory techniques are more effective and comfortable.

options.text: It is used only after cranial manipulation
options.rationale: It is not limited to use after cranial manipulation.

options.text: It is contraindicated with other OMT techniques
options.rationale: It is not contraindicated with other OMT.

question: Perpendicular stretching of a paraspinal muscle is best characterized by which statement about the direction of applied force?
cited_learning_objective: Describe the force direction of a perpendicular stretch.

options.text: Force is applied along the long axis, separating origin and insertion
options.rationale: Force along the long axis is a longitudinal stretch.

options.text: Force is applied across the long axis of the muscle fibers
options.rationale: Perpendicular stretching applies force across the long axis of the muscle fibers.

options.text: Force is a light circular gliding stroke over the skin
options.rationale: A light circular gliding stroke is effleurage.

options.text: Force is a deep kneading and squeezing of the muscle belly
options.rationale: Deep kneading is petrissage.

options.text: Force is a rhythmic percussive tapping over the muscle
options.rationale: Rhythmic tapping is tapotement.

question: Which of the following lists the four commonly described methods of soft tissue technique?
cited_learning_objective: List the four foundational soft tissue methods.

options.text: HVLA, BLT, counterstrain, and muscle energy
options.rationale: Those are other OMT methods, not the four soft tissue methods.

options.text: Traction, linear stretching, lateral stretching, and deep pressure
options.rationale: These are the four foundational methods of osteopathic soft tissue techniques in this chapter.

options.text: Skin rolling, effleurage, petrissage, and tapotement
options.rationale: Those are massage descriptions, not the four foundational methods keyed here.

options.text: Articulatory, cranial, visceral, and myofascial release
options.rationale: Those are not the four soft tissue methods.
Those are motions, not soft tissue methods.

question: Before treatment, a patient has a positive standing flexion test on the left, thought to be caused by lumbar muscle hypertonicity rather than a true bony pelvic dysfunction. Which post-treatment finding would best confirm that hypothesis?
cited_learning_objective: Confirm a false-positive standing flexion test.

options.text: The test remains positive on the left despite reduced left paraspinal tone
options.rationale: A test that stays positive despite reduced tone argues against the hypothesis.

options.text: The test becomes positive on the right after treatment
options.rationale: A new right-sided positive would not confirm the hypothesis.

options.text: The test resolves after left lumbar soft tissue treatment reduces erector spinae tone
options.rationale: If ipsilateral lumbar hypertonicity produced the false positive, reducing left erector spinae tone should resolve the test.

options.text: The pubic symphysis becomes tender to palpation
options.rationale: A tender pubic symphysis is not an expected confirmation.
Abolished sacroiliac motion is not an expected confirmation.

question: Which of the following describes effleurage?
cited_learning_objective: Define effleurage.

options.text: Lifting the skin into a roll and moving it along the body
options.rationale: That description is skin rolling.

options.text: A light stroking technique, often used to promote lymphatic drainage
options.rationale: Effleurage is a superficial gliding stroke that promotes circulation and lymphatic flow.

options.text: Kneading muscles in a rhythmic fashion
options.rationale: Kneading is petrissage.

options.text: Rhythmic striking of tissues with the side of the hand
options.rationale: Rhythmic striking is tapotement.

options.text: Sustained deep inhibitory pressure on a tender point
options.rationale: Sustained deep pressure is direct inhibition.

question: A student is asked to match each descriptor to its technique. Which of the following pairings is correct?
cited_learning_objective: Match one correct technique descriptor.

options.text: Light, gentle, circular superficial gliding is called tapotement
options.rationale: Light circular gliding is effleurage, not tapotement.

options.text: Steady, sustained, deep pressure held on a point is called effleurage
options.rationale: Steady sustained deep pressure is direct inhibition, not effleurage.

options.text: Rhythmic percussive tapping is called tapotement
options.rationale: Rhythmic percussive tapping is tapotement.

options.text: Rolling skin between thumb and fingers is called kneading
options.rationale: Rolling skin between thumb and fingers is skin rolling, not kneading.

options.text: Deep kneading and squeezing of the belly is called skin rolling
options.rationale: Deep kneading and squeezing is petrissage, not skin rolling.

question: Which of the following massage methods involves the kneading of muscles?
cited_learning_objective: Name the kneading method.

options.rationale: Petrissage kneads or squeezes muscles to mobilize tissue and improve circulation.
Effleurage is light stroking, not kneading.
Tapotement is percussion, not kneading.
Skin rolling lifts a skin fold, rather than kneading muscle.
Traction separates tissues along an axis, rather than kneading.

question: Four techniques are described by their mechanics. Which one is NOT a stretch-based method?
cited_learning_objective: Identify the method that is not a stretch.

options.text: Traction that lengthens the cervical extensors from origin to insertion
options.rationale: That is a longitudinal stretch.

options.text: Anterolateral displacement of the lumbar paraspinals against a counterforce
options.rationale: That is a transverse stretch.

options.text: Sustained inhibitory pressure held on a hypertonic suboccipital region
options.rationale: Sustained inhibitory pressure is direct inhibition, which is not a stretch.

options.text: Medial-to-lateral displacement of the thoracic erector spinae
options.rationale: That is a transverse stretch.

options.text: Longitudinal traction of the posterior cervical tissues
options.rationale: That is a longitudinal stretch.

question: Which of the following best describes tapotement?
cited_learning_objective: Define tapotement.

options.rationale: Kneading is petrissage.
Stroking is closer to effleurage.

options.text: Rhythmic striking, often with the side of the hand
options.rationale: Tapotement stimulates tissues through rhythmic alternating strikes.

options.text: Sustained deep pressure on a hypertonic muscle
options.rationale: Sustained deep pressure is direct inhibition.

options.text: Longitudinal separation of muscle origin and insertion
options.rationale: That is a longitudinal stretch.

question: During the prone lumbar application of the Unilateral Thoracic and Lumbar Paraspinal Soft Tissue Pressure with Transverse Stretch, which pair correctly matches each hand with its role?
cited_learning_objective: Assign each hand in the prone lumbar transverse stretch.

options.text: Superior hand: counterforce lift at the ASIS; inferior hand: anterolateral paraspinal pressure
options.rationale: This reverses the two hands.

options.text: Superior hand: anterolateral paraspinal pressure; inferior hand: counterforce lift at the ASIS
options.rationale: The superior hand applies anterior and lateral pressure to the lumbar paraspinals. The inferior hand lifts the ASIS as counterforce.

options.text: Superior hand: longitudinal traction of the spine; inferior hand: skin rolling
options.rationale: Longitudinal traction and skin rolling are not the roles in this technique.

options.text: Superior hand: direct inhibition of the psoas; inferior hand: tapotement
options.rationale: Psoas inhibition and tapotement are not used in this technique.

options.text: Superior hand: sacral rocking; inferior hand: cervical traction
options.rationale: Sacral rocking and cervical traction are not the roles in this technique.

question: Which of the following is most likely to relieve hypertonicity of the erector spinae muscle group?
cited_learning_objective: Choose the technique for erector spinae hypertonicity.

options.rationale: Upper extremity inhibitory pressure does not directly address the erector spinae.

options.text: Unilateral Thoracic and Lumbar Paraspinal Soft Tissue Pressure and Stretch, Lateral Recumbent with Counterforce
options.rationale: The lateral recumbent lumbar soft tissue technique with counterforce directly addresses the erector spinae.
Longitudinal arch springing is not the technique keyed for the erector spinae.
Effleurage is not the technique keyed as most effective for this group.
Tapotement is not the technique keyed as most effective for this group.

question: In the prone Unilateral Paraspinal Soft Tissue Pressure with Transverse Stretch, the anterior and lateral force applied from a medial contact on the erector spinae primarily produces which of the following?
cited_learning_objective: Name the stretch produced by anterolateral force from a medial contact.

options.text: A longitudinal stretch along the muscle's long axis
options.rationale: A longitudinal stretch would pull along the muscle axis.

options.text: A transverse stretch across the muscle fibers
options.rationale: Anterior and lateral force from a medial contact displaces the erector spinae across its fibers.

options.text: Direct inhibition of a single trigger point
options.rationale: Direct inhibition is sustained point pressure.
Percussive stimulation is tapotement.

options.text: Skin rolling of the superficial fascia
options.rationale: Skin rolling engages only superficial tissue.

question: When performing suboccipital soft tissue pressure and traction, the physician's finger pads should be placed:
cited_learning_objective: Place the finger pads for suboccipital traction.

options.text: Directly on the spinous process of C2
options.rationale: The contact is not on the C2 spinous process.

options.text: Inferior to the occiput, posterior to the arch of C1
options.rationale: The finger pads go in the space inferior to the occiput, posterior to the arch of the atlas (C1).
The mastoid processes are not the contact.
The sternocleidomastoid is not the contact.

options.text: At the lateral border of the scapula
options.rationale: The scapular border is not the contact.

question: Which of the following represents an appropriate principle when applying soft tissue techniques?
cited_learning_objective: Choose an appropriate dosing principle for soft tissue.

options.text: Apply a sudden, rapid stretch to force the tissues to release
options.rationale: A sudden rapid stretch is not the dosing principle.

options.text: Keep the direction and amount of force constant regardless of tissue response
options.rationale: Force is adjusted according to tissue response.

options.text: Use steady or rhythmic force while adjusting based on tissue feedback
options.rationale: Force should be steady or rhythmic and adjusted in intensity and direction according to palpatory feedback.

options.text: Always apply the maximum amount of pressure tolerated by the patient
options.rationale: Maximum tolerated pressure is not the principle.

options.text: Use only one hand position throughout treatment, regardless of technique
options.rationale: Hand position changes with the technique.

question: Which soft tissue method is NOT characterized by static sustained force applied directly to a hypertonic muscle?
cited_learning_objective: Identify the method that is not sustained force on muscle.

options.rationale: The packet groups traction with methods that apply direct force to a hypertonic muscle.
Lateral stretching applies direct force to muscle.
Longitudinal stretching applies direct force to muscle.
Inhibitory pressure is sustained force on a hypertonic muscle.

Skin rolling lifts and rolls a fold of skin and subcutaneous tissue. It assesses and mobilizes superficial fascia rather than applying static sustained force directly to a hypertonic muscle. The printed rationale continues past the last extracted line and was not completed.
